name: Linezolid
summary: Synthetic oxazolidinone active against MRSA and VRE; 100% oral bioavailability makes it a key IV-to-PO step-down option.
mechanism: Binds the 50S ribosomal subunit and prevents formation of the 70S initiation complex — a unique mechanism among protein-synthesis inhibitors.
pharmacodynamics: Time-dependent, bacteriostatic against most enterococci/staphylococci (bactericidal for streptococci); AUC/MIC best predicts response.

dosing.renalAdjustment: No adjustment for standard courses (metabolites accumulate in severe renal impairment — monitor)

safety.pregnancy: Limited data (category C) — use only if clearly needed
warnings: Serotonin syndrome with SSRIs/SNRIs/MAOIs (weak MAO inhibition)
Peripheral and optic neuropathy with prolonged use
monitoring: Serotonin-syndrome signs if co-prescribed serotonergic drugs

indications: MRSA pneumonia (HAP/VAP — preferred over vancomycin in some guidelines)
Oral step-down for resistant Gram-positive infections
clinicalPearls: 100% oral bioavailability — easy IV-to-PO switch at the same dose
Avoid with SSRIs/serotonergic agents — serotonin syndrome risk
good: Oral and IV MRSA/VRE coverage with excellent lung penetration.
bad: Myelosuppression and neuropathy with prolonged courses; serotonin-syndrome interactions; cost.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard infectious-disease/pharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
